memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "There was no food, however, in the whole region because the famine was severe; both Egypt and Canaan wasted away because of the famine. Joseph collected all the money that was to be found in Egypt and Canaan in payment for the grain they were buying, and he brought it to Pharaoh's palace. When the money of the people of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all Egypt came to Joseph and said, 'Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes? Our money is all gone.'" — Gen 47:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The famine strips everything away. The people bring their money, and then the money runs out, and they come back with empty hands saying, "Why should we die before your eyes?"

There is a terrible honesty in that moment. Money buys food until it doesn't. Every security we build has a limit, and hard times find it.

The Bible is not against money or planning; Joseph himself is the great planner of this story. But Scripture warns repeatedly against putting our confidence in wealth, because wealth cannot carry the full weight we tend to put on it. Paul told Timothy to warn the rich not to put their hope in something so uncertain, but in God, who richly provides (1 Tim 6:17).

The Egyptians only discovered the limits of their money when the famine went long enough. Most of us discover the limits of our securities the same way — not through argument, but through experience.

Better to learn it early and gently. Whatever you are quietly depending on to keep you safe, hold it honestly before God and ask whether you are trusting it more than Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you quietly relying on for security besides God?
2. Have you ever discovered the limits of something you trusted?
3. How would your decisions change if your hope rested fully in God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I confess how easily I trust in things that cannot finally hold me. Teach me to depend on You, who richly provides, and loosen my grip on false securities. Amen.
